name: admin_permission_set
description: Manages a DuploCloud AI Helpdesk permission set — a named grant of access that can be assigned to users via permission set groups. Access is expressed as hierarchical resource grants: allow and deny rules, each naming one node by its root-to-leaf path and the verbs, actions and cloud scopes granted or blocked there.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Name of the permission set.

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the permission set.

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Whether the permission set is active. Defaults to active when omitted.

attributes.name: metadata
attributes.description: Free-form key/value metadata.

attributes.name: resource_grants
attributes.description: Hierarchical resource grants — the only thing consulted when deciding what this permission set can reach. Two flat rule lists, `allow` and `deny`, each rule naming one node by its root-to-leaf path. A request for verb v on path P is resolved in this order: a deny rule on P or on any ancestor of P listing v blocks it, and blocks the whole subtree beneath it; otherwise an allow rule on P itself listing v permits it; otherwise an allow rule on an ancestor of P listing v with `allow_all_children` permits it; otherwise a `GET` is permitted when P is an ancestor of some allow rule's path, so the path down to a grant stays readable; otherwise the request is denied. A user's permission sets are pooled, so a deny in any one of them applies everywhere. Supersedes `allowed_workspaces`, and conflicts with it — a config may set one or the other, not both.

attributes.name: allow
attributes.description: Rules granting access. Each names one node and the verbs, actions and scopes allowed there.

attributes.name: path
attributes.description: Full root-to-leaf path of the node this rule grants access to. The FIRST segment is always a workspace and the LAST segment is the target; the segments between them are the containment chain down to it (environment, resource group, and the category segment a cloud resource sits under). Order matters — rules are matched by path prefix.

attributes.name: node_type
attributes.description: Access-node type of this segment: `Workspace`, `Environment`, `ResourceGroup`, a category (`AWS`, `Kubernetes`, `Terraform`) or a concrete resource type (`AwsSqsQueue`, `AWSRdsInstance`, `AppService`, …). The set is not fixed — it is built from the node types the platform registers, so a deployment's own list is what `GET /v1/aiservicedesk/admin/data/accessnodes/types` returns.

attributes.name: node_id
attributes.description: ID of the object this segment names. Category segments have no object of their own and take their fixed id instead (`aws`, `k8s`, `terraform`). `*` may appear only in the LAST segment, where it means the node type as a whole rather than one object — a first segment of `*` covers every workspace, and a trailing `<Type>` / `*` pair is the path a create of that type is checked against.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Display name of the node, cached on the rule for the console's benefit. Never used to decide access — `node_id` alone is authoritative — so it may safely be left out.

attributes.name: verbs
attributes.description: HTTP verbs this rule covers: `GET` (read and list), `PUT` (update), `POST` (create), `DELETE`, or `ALL` for the four together. Prefer `ALL` on its own — combining it with a single verb is accepted but redundant. `ALL` covers those four verbs and NO named action: actions are never implied by verbs and have to be listed in `actions` explicitly.

attributes.name: actions
attributes.description: Named actions granted at this path — the operations that are gated separately from plain CRUD, such as `aws.jit`, `aws.ssm`, `kubernetes.jit`, `kubernetes.reboot`, `secret.read`, `secret.write`, `terraform.execute` or `workspace.setting`. `*` matches every action registered for the node type; the actions a given type registers are listed by `GET /v1/aiservicedesk/admin/data/accessnodes/types`. Actions are NEVER implied by `verbs`: a rule with `verbs = ["ALL"]` and no `actions` grants the four CRUD verbs and not one action. `allow_all_children` cascades actions exactly as it cascades verbs.

attributes.name: scopes
attributes.description: IDs of the cloud scopes granted at this path, or `*` for every scope in the workspace — resolved when access is evaluated, so `*` also covers scopes added later. Read only from rules whose path ends at a workspace and ignored on any other rule, since a scope belongs to a workspace. This is what replaces the deprecated `allowed_workspaces[].allowed_scopes` / `denied_scopes`, which held regular expressions matched against scope NAMES: storing IDs keeps a grant intact across a rename, at the cost of no longer picking up new scopes automatically unless `*` is used.

attributes.name: allow_all_children
attributes.description: Whether the verbs and actions inherit to the target's entire subtree, including objects created after the grant. Leave it off to grant the target node alone. Creating inside a container needs it: the container is a proper prefix of the new object's path, so `POST` on the container only reaches that path when the subtree is covered — grant `POST` on `<Type>` / `*` directly instead to permit creates without opening the rest of the subtree.

attributes.name: deny
attributes.description: Rules blocking access. A deny beats every allow, including allows in the user's other permission sets, and always covers the target's whole subtree — verb-scoped denies remove just the listed verbs from it.

attributes.name: path
attributes.description: Full root-to-leaf path of the node this rule blocks access to. The FIRST segment is always a workspace and the LAST segment is the target; the segments between them are the containment chain down to it (environment, resource group, and the category segment a cloud resource sits under). Order matters — rules are matched by path prefix.

attributes.name: node_type
attributes.description: Access-node type of this segment: `Workspace`, `Environment`, `ResourceGroup`, a category (`AWS`, `Kubernetes`, `Terraform`) or a concrete resource type (`AwsSqsQueue`, `AWSRdsInstance`, `AppService`, …). The set is not fixed — it is built from the node types the platform registers, so a deployment's own list is what `GET /v1/aiservicedesk/admin/data/accessnodes/types` returns.

attributes.name: node_id
attributes.description: ID of the object this segment names. Category segments have no object of their own and take their fixed id instead (`aws`, `k8s`, `terraform`). `*` may appear only in the LAST segment, where it means the node type as a whole rather than one object — a first segment of `*` covers every workspace, and a trailing `<Type>` / `*` pair is the path a create of that type is checked against.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Display name of the node, cached on the rule for the console's benefit. Never used to decide access — `node_id` alone is authoritative — so it may safely be left out.

attributes.name: verbs
attributes.description: HTTP verbs this rule covers: `GET` (read and list), `PUT` (update), `POST` (create), `DELETE`, or `ALL` for the four together. Prefer `ALL` on its own — combining it with a single verb is accepted but redundant. `ALL` covers those four verbs and NO named action: actions are never implied by verbs and have to be listed in `actions` explicitly.

attributes.name: actions
attributes.description: Named actions blocked at this path — the operations that are gated separately from plain CRUD, such as `aws.jit`, `aws.ssm`, `kubernetes.jit`, `kubernetes.reboot`, `secret.read`, `secret.write`, `terraform.execute` or `workspace.setting`. `*` matches every action registered for the node type; the actions a given type registers are listed by `GET /v1/aiservicedesk/admin/data/accessnodes/types`. Actions are NEVER implied by `verbs`, so leaving this empty does not mean "no actions": empty together with `verbs = ["ALL"]` it blocks EVERY action in the subtree, while a non-empty set blocks only the actions named.

attributes.name: scopes
attributes.description: IDs of the cloud scopes blocked at this path, or `*` for every scope in the workspace — resolved when access is evaluated, so `*` also covers scopes added later. Read only from rules whose path ends at a workspace and ignored on any other rule, since a scope belongs to a workspace. This is what replaces the deprecated `allowed_workspaces[].allowed_scopes` / `denied_scopes`, which held regular expressions matched against scope NAMES: storing IDs keeps a grant intact across a rename, at the cost of no longer picking up new scopes automatically unless `*` is used.

attributes.name: allow_all_children
attributes.description: Ignored on a deny rule — a deny always covers its target's entire subtree. Present only so a rule reads the same on either side.

attributes.name: allowed_workspaces
attributes.description: Deprecated legacy workspace list — use `resource_grants` instead. Kept so configurations written before resource grants existed keep applying: the entries still round-trip and the backend still converts them once, but nothing reads them when deciding access. Being computed, dropping the block from a configuration leaves the stored list alone rather than clearing it; set it to `[]` in its own apply to empty it, since it cannot be set alongside `resource_grants`.
attributes.deprecated: Deprecated — migrate to resource_grants. Access is decided from resource_grants alone, so entries here grant nothing on their own; a one-time backend migration converts an existing list into the equivalent allow rules, after which it is inert. Express new intent as resource_grants — the two attributes conflict, so remove this one when adopting it.

attributes.name: workspace_id
attributes.description: ID of the workspace this entry applies to.

attributes.name: allowed_scopes
attributes.description: Deprecated — use the `scopes` set on a `resource_grants` allow rule instead. Scopes within the workspace this permission grants access to. Each entry may be a regex matched against scope names.
attributes.deprecated: Deprecated — migrate to the scopes set on a resource_grants allow rule whose path ends at the workspace. These are regular expressions matched against scope NAMES; grants hold scope ids, which survive a rename.

attributes.name: denied_scopes
attributes.description: Deprecated — use the `scopes` set on a `resource_grants` deny rule instead. Scopes within the workspace this permission blocks access to. Each entry may be a regex matched against scope names.
attributes.deprecated: Deprecated — migrate to the scopes set on a resource_grants deny rule whose path ends at the workspace. These are regular expressions matched against scope NAMES; grants hold scope ids, which survive a rename.

attributes.name: allowed_agents
attributes.description: Agents within the workspace this permission grants access to. Each entry may be a regex.

attributes.name: denied_agents
attributes.description: Agents within the workspace this permission blocks access to. Each entry may be a regex.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.description: Timestamp when the permission set was created (RFC 3339, normalized to UTC at second precision).

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.description: Timestamp when the permission set was last updated (RFC 3339, normalized to UTC at second precision).

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Version counter, incremented on each update.
